messages:
maria: Quick share from the throughput vs latency sweep across GPUs/regions for SSE (streaming) vs HTTP (non-streaming). uploaded charts: https://redwood.internal/bench/sse-http-gpu-sweep — p50/p95/p99 + tokens/s by region and kernel. TL;DR: streaming gives much better first-token latency, HTTP wins on bulk throughput when we can batch. :bar_chart:

devin: Could you drop the short table here? curious about H100 vs A10G and region differences (us-west1 vs eu-west1 vs ap-southeast1).

maria: Sure — pasted the compact summary below (seq_len=128, batch policy: adaptive up to 32, kernel=triton/flash where applicable). Numbers are averaged over 10 runs. All times in ms, throughput = tokens/sec.

maria: ```
model: rw-large-v1 (fp16)
GPU  | endpoint  | region        | p50  | p95  | p99  | tokens/s
H100  | streaming | us-west1      | 18   | 42   | 110  | 920
H100  | http      | us-west1      | 62   | 120  | 270  | 1250
A10G  | streaming | us-west1      | 28   | 75   | 190  | 680
A10G  | http      | us-west1      | 88   | 190  | 420  | 960
H100  | streaming | eu-west1      | 22   | 52   | 130  | 870
H100  | http      | eu-west1      | 70   | 140  | 320  | 1180
A100  | streaming | ap-southeast1 | 26   | 60   | 150  | 740
A100  | http      | ap-southeast1 | 95   | 210  | 460  | 1000
```

maria: Notes: p50 is first-token latency for streaming, end-to-end for HTTP; HTTP measurements include request/response serialization. streaming p50 here is arrival of first chunk.

benchbot: Automated note: quantized int8 run (same config) increased tokens/s by ~1.7x on A10G but raised p99 variance on streaming by ~15%. raw artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/1769876543/int8/

kyle: Kernel stuff — we tried FlashAttention where supported on H100 and Triton kernels on A10G. Flash gave ~8-12% p50 improvement for streaming on H100. On A10G triton tuned kernels improved http throughput by ~10%.

alok: Interesting regional delta — us-west1 latency + throughput consistently best (lower RTT + newer instance families). ap-southeast1 shows higher p99 on http due to serialization overhead + lower networking. Can we try prefilling KV cache to see effect on http batching?

devin: For the product team decision: if customers want snappy first-response for chat UX pick streaming (ws/sse) on H100 or A100 in us-west1; if they want max cost-efficiency for high-throughput ingestion (embeddings-like or long batched generation) pick http with higher batching and A10G/T4 pools.

maria: Action items:
- run KV-prefill sweep for http/batch sizes 8/16/32 (assigned @kyle)
- run int8 stability check on streaming p99 (assigned @benchbot)
- add routing policy experiment that pins streaming to H100 pool in us-west1 and falls back to http/A10G in other regions (assigned @sre-bot)

kyle: starting KV-prefill runs now, will post incremental charts in this thread.

benchbot: queued int8 streaming stability job (job id: 2026-03-20-67342). will post p99 histograms when done.

maria: thanks — will update the team doc with recommended defaults and the charts link. ping me for quick demo. :thumbsup:
